title: Basic couching
subtitle: Holding a laid thread to the fabric surface with tiny binding stitches
excerpt: Couching lays one thread along a line and stitches it down with a finer binding thread, placing each binding stitch at regular intervals to hold the laid thread flat.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), couching chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), couching entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The thread placed along the surface of the fabric to form the couched line. It is held down by binding stitches and does not pass through the fabric except at its start and end points.
A small stitch that passes over a laid thread and into the fabric, holding the laid thread in position.

heroPrompt: Basic couching on linen, a thick laid thread held down by evenly spaced binding stitches, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Couching lets you use threads too heavy or irregular to pass through the fabric. The
lies on top, anchored at each end by passing through the fabric with a large needle. A finer needle and thread then sews it down with small right-angle

items.label: Laid thread
items.value: Perle cotton no. 5, wool, or ribbon

items.label: Binding thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands, matching or contrasting colour

items.label: Needles
items.value: Large needle for laid thread, embroidery needle size 9 for binding

content.text: Thread the large needle with the laid thread. Bring it up at the start of the line.
Lay the thread along the drawn line and hold it with your non-stitching hand. At the end of the line, insert the needle back through the fabric.
Thread the binding needle. Bring it up just to one side of the laid thread near the start. Work a small stitch over the laid thread and back into the fabric on the other side.
Repeat at even intervals of 4 to 6 mm along the entire length. Keep binding stitches at right angles to the laid thread.

items.symptom: The laid thread waves rather than following the line
items.cause: Binding stitches too far apart near curves.
items.fix: Add binding stitches closer together on curves: every 2 to 3 mm around tight bends.

items.symptom: Binding stitches are visible and interrupt the line
items.cause: Binding thread is too thick relative to the laid thread.
items.fix: Use a single strand or a finer matching thread for the binding.

content.text: Basic couching is the base for bricked couching, laid work, and goldwork. In goldwork, metal threads that cannot pierce the fabric are held down by fine binding stitches.
